symptom: After the v1 BSON driver removal (ako/mxcli#1497), go.mod no longer named github.com/klauspost/compress and `go list -m github.com/klauspost/compress` reported v1.19.2, the version a customer's Sonatype scan had blocked on for GHSA-fpmh-frq8-7rj8. No build, test or CI job failed
cause: The v1.20.3 floor from ako/mxcli#1493 was a hand-written `// indirect` require line for a module no mxcli package imports (it arrives through mongo-driver/v2, used only for its BSON packages). `go mod tidy` removes any requirement that no package in the module's import graph needs, so the first tidy after it, the one #1497 ran to drop v1, deleted the line and MVS fell back to the v1.19.2 mongo-driver/v2@v2.9.2 declares
file: `internal/depfloor/floor.go` (new, `//go:build depfloor`, blank-imports github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd); `internal/depfloor/floor_test.go` (new, TestGoModKeepsSecurityFloors); `go.mod`/`go.sum` (klauspost/compress v1.20.3, now direct)
insight: A security floor on a module the program never imports is not a go.mod edit, it is an import: tidy treats every build tag except `ignore` as enabled, so a blank import behind a tag no build sets keeps the requirement through tidy while compiling nothing (`go version -m bin/mxcli` still lists no klauspost/compress). Measured both ways: a hand-added require line is gone after one `go mod tidy`; with floor.go deleted tidy drops the line and the test fails 'go.mod does not require'; with floor.go present but no version pinned tidy re-adds it at the graph's v1.19.2 and the test fails 'below the floor'. The guard reads go.mod, which is what the scanner's graph is built from, and a direct requirement at or above the floor guarantees MVS selects at least that version
